questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.question: The rotational analogue of mass in linear motion is:
questions.explanation: Moment of inertia (I) resists changes in rotational motion, performing the exact same role as mass (m) in translational motion.
questions.ncertReference: Physics Class 11, Chapter 7: System of Particles and Rotational Motion

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: How does acceleration due to gravity (g) change as we move above the surface of Earth?
questions.explanation: Acceleration due to gravity g' = g / (1 + h/R)². As height h increases, g decreases.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: What is the pH of pure neutral water at 25°C?
questions.explanation: At 25°C, [H⁺] = 10⁻⁷ M in pure water. Therefore, pH = -log(10⁻⁷) = 7.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In the reaction Zn + Cu²⁺ → Zn²⁺ + Cu, which species undergoes oxidation?
questions.explanation: Zinc loses 2 electrons (oxidation state goes from 0 to +2), so Zn undergoes oxidation.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: Roots that arise from parts of the plant other than the radicle are termed as:
questions.explanation: Roots developing from any part of the plant other than the embryonic radicle are adventitious roots (e.g., banyan tree, maize).
questions.ncertReference: Biology Class 11, Chapter 5: Morphology of Flowering Plants

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: Which plant tissue is responsible for transport of water and minerals from roots to leaves?
questions.explanation: Xylem is a complex permanent tissue that conducts water and dissolved minerals unidirectionally from roots to stems and leaves.
questions.ncertReference: Biology Class 11, Chapter 6: Anatomy of Flowering Plants

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: Which cell type in human blood is responsible for clotting?
questions.explanation: Thrombocytes (platelets) release factors essential for blood coagulation.
questions.ncertReference: Biology Class 11, Chapter 18: Body Fluids and Circulation

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: The functional unit of the human kidney is called:
questions.explanation: Each human kidney contains roughly 1 million tubular structures called nephrons, which serve as functional filtration units.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The kinetic energy of a body becomes how many times if its velocity is doubled?
questions.explanation: Kinetic Energy KE = 1/2 m v². Since KE is proportional to v², doubling v increases KE by 2² = 4 times.
questions.ncertReference: Physics Class 11, Chapter 6: Work, Energy and Power

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Organic Chemistry - Some Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.question: Which effect involves complete transfer of a shared pair of π-electrons to one of the atoms in the presence of an attacking reagent?
questions.explanation: The electromeric effect (E effect) is a temporary effect operating only in the presence of an attacking reagent involving π-electron transfer.
questions.ncertReference: Chemistry Class 11, Chapter 12: Organic Chemistry - Basic Principles
